policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'and great in power' is compatible with both the qere וּגְדָל and the ketiv וגדול; no mapped textual note distinguishes them, so the base qere remains the fallback.

ASV 'shall no more pass through thee' is compatible with both the qere לַֽעֲבָר and the ketiv לעבור. The mapped note is classed alternative_rendering and concerns 'the wicked one,' so it does not decide this reading; the base qere remains the fallback.
